title: RAND: bit-exact 16-bit LFSR
alt: JavaScript rand() function: a 16-bit linear feedback shift register matching the 6502 RAND routine

title: Radix misinterpretation (EFIRE)
alt: The 6502 line LDA I,10. under .RADIX 16 means decimal 10; version 1 generated 18, version 2 corrects it to 10

title: BCD score threshold (ENEMY)
alt: The 6502 compare CMP I,30 on the BCD high byte means 30,000 points; version 1 used 3000, version 2 uses 30000

title: Bitmask cadence (EFIRE)
alt: 6502 code loading FRAME, shifting left with ASL and branching if not zero, which fires every 128 frames
code:
; EFIRE routine:
LDA FRAME
ASL
BNE 10$

title: Two-player turn switch fix (checkWave)
alt: checkWave() turn transition that sets ship.sdelay to 0x10 so the next player's ship appears after 16 ticks

title: POST /v1/systemone: request and response (abridged)
alt: A typed request with a state sentence and four action criteria, and the response with the chosen action and its confidence
code:
POST /v1/systemone
{ "state": "Situation: Danger. large rock is incoming from the right on a
             collision path in 21 ticks. Pilot needs to turn left and thrust
             to dodge.",
  "questions": { "action": {
    "type": "choice",
    "instructions": "Determine the required flight action for the spaceship.",
    "criteria": {
      "stay_and_fire":
        "Safe situation. Aim weapons towards target rock and fire.",
      "turn_left_and_thrust":
        "Asteroid on right side. Turn left and thrust away to dodge.",
      "turn_right_and_thrust":
        "Asteroid on left side. Turn right and thrust away to dodge.",
      "hyperspace":
        "Fatal emergency when collision is unavoidable. Hyperspace escape jump." } } } }

->  { "answers": { "action": { "choice": "turn_left_and_thrust",
                               "probabilities": { ... }, "confidence": 0.97 } } }
label: HTTP and JSON

title: Same request without the verdict (prompt level facts, abridged)
alt: A request whose state sentence lists objects with distance, bearing and time to impact, and whose options describe only the action
code:
POST /v1/systemone
{ "state": "Ship speed 1.2 px/tick. Nearest objects:
             1) large rock, 640 units away, 35 deg right of the nose,
                closing at 18 px/tick, impact in 36 ticks;
             2) medium rock, 910 units away, 120 deg left of the nose,
                moving away at 4 px/tick.",
  "questions": { "action": {
    "type": "choice",
    "instructions": "Choose the action that keeps the ship alive while it
                     destroys rocks and saucers.",
    "criteria": {
      "stay_and_fire":         "Keep the current course and keep aiming and shooting at rocks.",
      "turn_left_and_thrust":  "Rotate left and accelerate.",
      "turn_right_and_thrust": "Rotate right and accelerate.",
      "hyperspace":            "Jump to a random place on the screen. The jump can destroy the ship." } } } }

title: The student3 request: geometry only, four strategies (abridged from the training file)
label: HTTP and JSON
alt: A typed request whose state text lists the nearest objects with distance, bearing, closing speed and closest approach, and four strategy options, with the response naming one strategy
code:
POST /v1/systemone
{ "state": "The ship moves at 3.6 units/tick, 86 deg right of the nose.
             Nearest objects:
             1) saucer torpedo, 166 units away, 3 deg left of the nose,
                closing at 13.6 units/tick, closest approach 111 units,
                51 deg left of the nose in 7 ticks;
             2) small saucer, 711 units away, 49 deg left of the nose,
                moving away at 15.1 units/tick; a torpedo fired now meets
                it in 16 ticks if aimed 69 deg left of the nose;
             3) ... 4) ...",
  "questions": { "action": {
    "type": "choice",
    "instructions": "Which strategy should the ship follow for the next
                     second to stay alive and destroy rocks and saucers?",
    "criteria": {
      "aim":        "Hold the ship in place. Turn to the target a torpedo can
                     reach soonest and fire when lined up. No thrust.",
      "escape":     "Fly the thrust manoeuvre that takes the ship out of the
                     path of the objects, and fire at whatever is lined up
                     on the way.",
      "brake":      "Thrust against the ship's drift until it is nearly still,
                     and fire at whatever is lined up on the way.",
      "hyperspace": "Press the hyperspace key, which jumps to a random place
                     on the screen. The jump can destroy the ship." } } } }

->  { "answers": { "action": { "choice": "aim | escape | brake | hyperspace",
                               "probabilities": { ... } } } }

title: The executor: the code flies the chosen strategy every tick (abridged from spExecute)
alt: The four strategies and the spExecute function: hyperspace pulses the key, escape runs the dodge search, brake plans a thrust against the drift, and every strategy ends in the same steering call

title: The student pilot: ask when idle, fly every tick, fall back when offline (abridged from strategyPilot)
alt: The strategyPilot function: a non-blocking request when none is pending, the answer stored as the held strategy, a fallback to smartPilot when the server is offline, and spExecute called on every tick
